prefix.content: In this session, ANSI-specific output tests should set color=True on CliRunner.invoke, assert an expected styling escape as well as the readable text, and leave production color defaults unchanged. This is not a rule to colorize all output tests.
Understood. I will keep that rule scoped to these tests.
Test a command that already prints Ready using green click.secho output. Add a regression that verifies the green ANSI styling survives capture, without changing the command.
I drafted runner.invoke(status, []) without a color option and checked only Ready. I also sketched adding color=True to the production secho call globally if the styling assertion fails.
What concrete next test plan will you follow before touching those files?

last_user_turn: What concrete next test plan will you follow before touching those files?

convention.title: Preserve ANSI at the runner boundary for a color-specific assertion
points: Invoke the styled command with CliRunner.invoke(color=True) so ANSI escapes are preserved for this test.
Assert both the expected ANSI styling escape and the semantic output text.
Keep production styling behavior unchanged; do not globally force color or alter the command merely to satisfy the test.
convention.scope: Tests specifically asserting Click styled output and ANSI preservation; not ordinary plain-output tests or global color policy.

held_out_correction: We already scoped this to the test runner: set color=True on invoke, assert the green escape and Ready text, and do not change production styling defaults.
